Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the final session of Day 1! The umpires and Indian players have already taken their positions. Out walk the Aussie opening pair - Usman Khawaja and Nathan McSweeney. Jasprit Bumrah has the new ball and is raring to go. Here we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Well then, with the Indian innings drawing to a close, TEA has been taken. Australia will come out to bat after the break and they have a huge opportunity to replicate the same dominance with the bat. They know that the Indian pace attack is a bit inexperienced comparatively and with Jadeja and Ashwin absent as well, it will be a steep hill for the tourists to climb from here. It will require a miraculous bowling display from India against this experienced Aussie batting unit. Stay tuned, as we will be back with the Australian innings, right after a few minutes from now.

Losing on the momentum built by Pant and Reddy, India's vulnerability was exposed yet again with another monumental collapse with India slipping down from 128/7 to 150 all out. For Australia, Josh Hazlewood was the most successful bowler as he never let the Indian batters get off the blocks and snagged a spectacular 4-fer with Starc, Cummins, and Marsh all chipping in with a couple of wickets each. All ten wickets were shared by the Aussie pace quartet that troubled the Indians right, left and centre. For India, Nitish Kumar Reddy was the highest run scorer and did really well for his brisk 41.

With Lyon struggling to find his rhythm and Pant taking the attack against him, Cummins smartly moved back to an all-pace attack. Reddy, in particular, impressed with his defensive technique and struck a few boundaries too. Just as Pant was threatening to convert his start into something substantial, Cummins struck, snuffing out the dangerous left-hander, and also redeeming himself from a dropped catch earlier.

The Australian camp opened with Mitchell Marsh joining the bowling attack, as Cummins maintained his aggressive all-pace strategy to build on the morning dominance. The tactic paid off when 'The Bison' struck twice in quick intervals, which left India reeling with half their side back in the sheds on a very sorry-looking score. The tide, however, began to slightly turn as conditions eased, with Pant finally finding his groove. He and Reddy crafted a gutsy partnership, mixing solid defense with bold strokeplay.

In an attempt to weather the storm, Pant and Jurel resumed their innings for India. Despite the second session usually favoring batters, they approached the ruthless Australian pacers with caution. Jurel showed early promise with some confident boundaries, but his innings was cut short by a catch in the slips. Pant struggled to find his rhythm, reflecting the overall uncertainty plaguing the Indian batting lineup.

India's innings never found its feet, with familiar top-order frailties coming back to haunt them. While KL Rahul fought a lone battle trying to hold the top order, wickets tumbled at the other end. Even the usually reliable Kohli couldn't weather the storm, and his early departure heaped even more pressure on an already strained and inexperienced lower middle order. India were badly reduced to a paltry 59/5 with the hosts bossing up the first session.

A pure action-packed phase of play as compared to the morning session. It had everything - Aussie pace dominance at full tilt, a resilient Pant-Nitish stand and in between and then the pacers squeezing back in to close in the session bundling India out. This post-Lunch session has moved this inaugural Test at a rapid pace courtesy of the Aussie pace battery being threateningly dangerous and doing the basic things correctly.

Right then, India find themselves up against it early in the Test. A lot will rest on the shoulders of Pant, considering that Jurel and Nitish Kumar Reddy are playing their first Test in Australia. On the other hand, Australia will want to maintain the same intensity and continue doing what they did in the first session. They just kept things simple and were consistent in hitting the right areas to reap the rewards. Do join us back at 5 am GMT for the start of the second session. See you then. Cheers!

Virat Kohli's stay at the crease was brief as he became Hazlewood's second victim of the day. Amidst this, KL Rahul showcased immense patience and decisiveness in his shot selection and defense. Just when it seemed Rahul and Pant were steadying the innings, Starc broke the partnership with a contentious caught-behind decision. Initially given not out by the on-field umpire, the Australians reviewed successfully, with the third umpire finding enough evidence to overturn the decision.

Well, a thoroughly dominant morning for Australia! Despite losing the toss, they seized control of the first session with a masterful display of pace bowling, leaving India reeling under relentless pressure. After opting to bat first, India were rocked early when Mitchell Starc dismissed Yashasvi Jaiswal for a duck. Coming in at number three, Devdutt Padikkal never seemed comfortable at the crease, struggling to capitalize on the rare loose deliveries that the Australian pace trio offered.

Commentary.Commentary: Goosebumps, right? Well, that's the magnitude of excitement for this series across the globe. Done with the pre-match formalities and it is now time for action to begin in this 'West Test' at Perth. Scatteringly cloudy skies welcome the two Indian openers. Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul walk out to the middle. Mitchell Starc has the new red Kookaburra cherry in his hand and is all in readiness to kick off the proceedings. Let's play...

Right then, just a few moments away from the commencement of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy. Australian legend Allan Border and the Indian stalwart Sunil Gavaskar walk out with the glittering trophy in their hands. They carefully place it on the podium. Now, the two sets of players walk out for their respective national anthems. It will be India's first, followed by the national anthem of Australia.

The captain of Australia, Pat Cummins says that they were a bit sceptical as to what to do. He adds that they are pretty happy either way. Shares that they have had a couple of months of build up and they can't wait to get started. Feels that they are well placed as a team before the start of this series. Mentions that any format they play against India is always fiercely fought. Tells that the wickets here in Perth are nice and bouncy and that is what you want as a pacer.

The stand-in captain of India, Jasprit Bumrah says it looks like a good wicket and says they are very confident. Adds they had great practice sessions coming into this series. He also says that they played a Test here in 2018 and they very well know what to expect from this pitch. He mentions that it gets quicker as the game progresses. Informs Nitish Kumar Reddy makes his Test debut as the fast-bowling all rounder. Tells they have four seamers along with Washington Sundar as the only spinner.

India (Playing XI) - KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal, Virat Kohli, Rishabh Pant (WK), Dhruv Jurel, Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy (On debut), Harshit Rana (On debut), Jasprit Bumrah (C), Mohammed Siraj.

Australia (Playing XI) - Usman Khawaja, Nathan McSweeney (On debut), Marnus Labuschagne, Steven Smith, Travis Head, Mitchell Marsh, Alex Carey (WK), Pat Cummins (C), Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon, Josh Hazlewood.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favour of India. Jasprit Bumrah opts to BAT first.

JUST IN - Nitish Kumar Reddy has been handed his maiden Test cap by Virat Kohli. There will be another debutant in the Indian camp with Harshit Rana also making his debut. The right-arm seamer, Rana has received his cap from Ravichandran Ashwin. So, two debutants for India and one in the form of Nathan McSweeney for Australia.

Right then, the tension is palpable as two giants of the game embark on what could be another historical journey and amidst all of it, Nathan McSweeney has just been presented the 'baggy green' by Darren Lehmann as he is all set to make his Test debut. Stick around as the all-important toss isn't far away now.

When India were bundled out for just 36 runs in the second innings of the opening game of this series last time around, no one anticipated the comeback and this time, they are yet again under the pump just before the opening game. A 3-0 loss at home to the Kiwis and a couple of crucial players set to miss the opening Test could just be the catalyst that this Indian side needs in order to find its best form but it won't be easy against this Aussie bowling attack.

The Aussie summer is always a time which cricketing fans wait religiously and it's for matches like these. For hosts, Australia it is an opportunity to take revenge of the last home series against India that saw them being handed a taste of their own medicine. This time around though, Pat Cummins and co will be raring to go and will have a full-strength squad to boast as well but that batting line-up could prove to be a tad fragile against quality bowlers.

Hello, hello! A very warm welcome to wherever you are across the globe. It is 'D-Day,' the day that marks the start of cricket's most-talked about rivalry in recent years - the Border-Gavaskar Trophy. It may not have the history like the Ashes but the competitive spirit is second to none and it all starts here at the Perth Stadium just a few minutes away from the iconic WACA stadium and truth be told, the new stadium still has a lot of spice to offer as Australia and India embark on a highly-anticipated five-Test series.
